newsitem.title: GERMANY: Revaluing gold would hamper Buba policy - Jochimsen.
newsitem.headline: Revaluing gold would hamper Buba policy - Jochimsen.

text.p: Bundesbank council member Reimut Jochimsen said on Friday that the German government's plans to revalue Bundesbank currency and gold reserves would constrain the central bank's activities in the run-up to EMU.

Stressing the Bundesbank's deep opposition to the plan, Jochimsen told Reuters the central bank might at most consider a partial reserve revaluation, and profit payout, in 1998, once a decision had been reached on which states launch the euro.

"The Bundesbank needs complete freedom to manoeuvre in 1997 and 1998. It would be completely contradictory to try to limit this freedom though a request to revalue currency reserves and to distribute the profits from the new valuation," he said.
Jochimsen, speaking in a telephone interview, also said that the government's plans to revalue gold and currency reserves would actually end up causing overall interest rates to rise.
The government has said it hopes its interest payments would be lowered by the revaluation measure, since the profit from the revaluation could be used to retire old debt.
"The lasting damage which the realisation of the gold plans would bring is far greater than the short-term financial benefit it is calculated to achieve," Jochimsen warned.

The Bundesbank would only consider a partial revaluation in 1998 if it became clear by then under what conditions central banks in Europe would transfer currency reserves to the future European Central Bank and if there were clear indications that the euro would be stable.
That revaluation would form part of the Bundesbank's regular annual accounts, Jochimsen said.
Jochimsen said Waigel's plans envisaged valuing gold reverces at their market price, minus 40 percent.
Currency reserves, on the other hand, would be revalued at their market price without any discount under the proposal, he said, although there would be risk reserves.
"The plan is to revalue currency reserves at a particular date without any discount whatsoever," he said.
